message.content:
In computer‑vision pipelines, “purple” is nothing more than a particular combination of red, green and blue (or hue, saturation, value) values.  It has no intrinsic semantic meaning unless you decide to give it one.

Typical uses include:

| Use case | Why purple is chosen | How it’s encoded |
|----------|---------------------|------------------|
| **Segmentation mask** | A distinct, rarely‑used hue so that different classes don’t overlap visually | Often a single RGB triplet such as (128, 0, 128) or HSV (300°, 1.0, 0.5) |
| **Highlighting keypoints / bounding boxes** | Stands out against common backgrounds (e.g., natural scenes) | Same RGB/HSV values, sometimes with alpha transparency |
| **Data augmentation** | Randomly recoloring objects to test robustness | Randomly sampled hue around 300° ± 10° |
| **Visualization of feature maps** | Color‑coding activation levels | Map activation intensity to a purple‑to‑white gradient |

So in short, purple in computer vision is simply a convenient, visually distinctive color value that you can use to encode labels, highlight regions, or augment data. Its “meaning” comes from how you choose to interpret it in your application.
